name: CRAI Content Updater
author: mark456321

sections.description:
CRAI Content Updater keeps your WordPress content accurate, competitive, and ranking.

Over time, blog posts go stale: prices change, statistics become outdated, year references age, and SEO meta loses relevance. CRAI Content Updater uses the AI provider of your choice to research current facts and refresh outdated content — saving every change as a draft for your review before anything goes live.

Your original content never changes without your approval.

How It Works

  1. Pick any published post or page from the Refresh Content tab
  2. Choose what to update: facts, dates, prices, reviews, SEO metadata, or tone
  3. The AI reads, diagnoses, and refreshes your content, saving it as a draft
  4. Review the changes, approve, and the live post updates — or discard it

Key Features

  • Unlimited Content Refreshes — Refresh as many posts as you want, as often as you want. No caps, no monthly limits, no license keys.
  • Draft Review Workflow — Every update saves as a draft. Your live post never changes until you explicitly approve it.
  • Multi-Provider Support — Works with Claude (Anthropic), OpenAI (GPT-4o), Gemini Paid, and Gemini Free. Bring your own API key.
  • Gemini Free Built-In — Works out of the box with a free Google Gemini API key. No credit card required to get started.
  • Bulk Refresh — Select multiple posts and refresh them sequentially in the background.
  • Freshness Scoring — Posts sorted by staleness so you always know what needs attention first.
  • Elementor Support — Widget-by-widget updates preserve your Elementor layout.
  • Update History — Full log of every AI refresh with before/after word counts and change summaries.
  • Performance Analytics — Track post-refresh view trends with built-in pageview tracking (no third-party services).

What Can Be Refreshed

  • Dates and time references — “in 2022” -> “currently”
  • Facts, statistics, and data — outdated figures updated with current values
  • Prices and product information — pricing and feature lists kept current
  • Review scores and ratings — star ratings, pros/cons, verdicts updated
  • SEO title and meta description — rewritten with current year and keyword
  • Tone and readability — shorter paragraphs, active voice, filler words removed

External Services

This plugin connects to AI provider APIs to perform content analysis and rewriting. AI processing happens on the provider’s servers — that is the core function of the plugin.

You choose which provider to use and supply your own API key. Supported providers:

  • Anthropic Claude — anthropic.com · Terms of Service · Privacy Policy
  • OpenAI — openai.com · Terms of Service · Privacy Policy
  • Google Gemini (paid and free tier) — ai.google.dev · Terms of Service · Privacy Policy

What is sent: When you trigger a refresh, the plugin sends the post title, post content, focus keyword (if available), and your selected update preferences to the AI provider you have configured. The provider’s response is saved locally as a WordPress draft.

What is NOT sent: Nothing is sent to CRAI servers. API keys and post content stay between your site and the AI provider you select. The plugin does not phone home, collect telemetry, or transmit any data to third parties beyond your chosen AI provider.

API keys are stored in the WordPress options table on your own database.

Pro Version

A separate, paid Pro plugin is available at contentrefreshai.com. The Pro plugin is hosted independently — it is not part of, and not unlockable from, this free plugin. The free plugin’s code is fully functional with no hidden or locked features.

Requirements

  • An API key from your chosen AI provider (Google Gemini has a free tier — no credit card required)
  • WordPress 5.8 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
sections.installation:
Automatic Installation

  1. Go to Plugins -> Add New
  2. Search for “CRAI Content Updater”
  3. Click Install Now then Activate

Manual Installation

  1. Download the plugin zip
  2. Go to Plugins -> Add New -> Upload Plugin
  3. Upload and activate

Setup

After activation a notice will appear with a link to Settings. Add your AI provider API key and you’re ready to go. Google Gemini has a free tier — no credit card required.
sections.faq:
Do I need my own AI API key?

Yes. You supply your own API key from Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google. Google Gemini has a free tier that works well for most sites — no credit card required.

Are there any usage limits inside the plugin?

No. This plugin has no refresh limits, no license activation, no time trials, no quotas. Refresh as many posts as often as you want.

The only practical limits come from the AI provider you choose — for example, Google’s free Gemini tier has lower request rates and a smaller output token cap than the paid Gemini API. The plugin shows a warning when the free Gemini tier is active so you know what to expect. Paid providers have higher limits set by the provider.

Does it change my live posts automatically?

Never. Every AI refresh saves as a private draft. Your live post only updates when you explicitly approve the draft.

Is my content sent anywhere other than the AI provider?

No. Your post content is sent only to the AI provider API you configure. Nothing is sent to CRAI servers or anywhere else.

Does the plugin work with Elementor?

Yes. The plugin detects Elementor posts and performs widget-by-widget updates to preserve your layout.

Which AI providers are supported?

Claude (Anthropic), GPT-4o (OpenAI), Gemini 1.5 Pro / 2.0 Flash / 2.5 Flash / 2.5 Pro (Google paid), and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite (Google free tier).
sections.changelog:
2.4.7

  • Removed all remaining Pro/creator feature code remnants to fully comply with WordPress.org Guideline 5 (Trialware): removed the creator-article branch from the draft approval handler, removed crai_creator_log option references, removed creator CSS classes, removed dead crai_publish_article JS handler, and simplified the draft review and history UI to refresh-only.
  • Fixed output escaping on six additional unescaped number_format() and ternary string echoes in the admin UI.
  • Removed leftover dead variables ($remaining, $used, $can_update, $is_complete) that were holdovers from the old Freemius update-counting system.
  • Removed a stale comment referencing update counting in approve_draft().

2.4.6

  • Removed Plugin URI from the main file header to resolve a WordPress.org submission error caused by Plugin URI and Author URI pointing to the same page. Author URI is retained as the canonical project URL.

2.4.5

  • Renamed plugin folder and text domain from crai-content-updater-free to crai-content-updater to match the approved WordPress.org slug.
  • Set the Author header to a real person name (Mark Proszowski) and added the wordpress.org Contributors username.
  • Replaced the truncated LICENSE.txt notice with the full GPL-2.0 license text.
  • Tightened the plugin description in the main file header to remove standalone Pro promotion (Pro information remains on the dedicated Upgrade tab as a clearly-labeled advertisement, which is allowed under Guideline 5).

2.4.4

  • Fixed: the performance views table (wp_crai_post_views) was never being created on plugin activation because no register_activation_hook was wired to CRAI_Performance::create_table(). Activation hook is now registered correctly at the top of the main plugin file. Added a lazy safety net (maybe_create_table) that auto-creates the table on the first admin page load if it’s missing, so users upgrading from an earlier version that never had the table created will recover automatically without needing to deactivate/reactivate.
  • Wrapped sum_views() and maybe_record_view() in wpdb->suppress_errors() so a missing table fails silently with a 0 return rather than dumping “table doesn’t exist” errors into the debug log on every public page view.

2.4.3

  • Fixed three SQL queries in the Performance class (CREATE TABLE, INSERT INTO, SELECT views) where // phpcs:ignore comments had been written inside the SQL string literal instead of next to the PHP code. MySQL was receiving the comment text as part of the query and throwing a syntax error during draft approval (when the baseline view-count snapshot is captured). Performance baseline capture now works correctly.
  • Wrapped CRAI_Performance::render_card() output with wp_kses_post() instead of using a phpcs suppression comment.

2.4.2

  • Fixed 6 output-escaping issues flagged by Plugin Check: wrapped crai_render_sentence_diff() output with wp_kses_post(), escaped $diff_color in inline CSS via esc_attr(), and wrapped four sprintf('%+.1f%%', ...) view-lift percentages with esc_html().

2.4.1

  • Added a dedicated “Upgrade to Pro” tab in the sidebar — a clearly-labeled advertisement page describing what the separate, paid CRAI Pro plugin (hosted independently at contentrefreshai.com) offers. The page opens with an explicit disclosure that it is an advertisement for a separate product and that nothing in the free plugin is locked or unlockable.

2.4.0

  • Removed all references to locked, gated, or disabled “Pro” features from the plugin code and UI to comply with WordPress.org Plugin Directory Guideline 5 (Trialware). The free plugin is now fully functional with no hidden or restricted built-in features.
  • Removed the dead “Create Article” navigation item, the “More options in CRAI Pro” upsell box, the “Pro Options” greyed-out checkbox lists in the refresh modal and bulk options panel, the Deep Research “Pro” badge, and the “Create New Article” Pro quick action from the dashboard.
  • Removed the unused class-crai-site-links.php Pro feature stub.
  • Removed the dead Content Creator settings card (Pexels, Unsplash, Pixabay, Stability AI key fields and the related image-source selector) — the image-generation feature itself was never wired up in the free plugin.
  • Removed the dead two-stage Deep Research code path (~410 lines) and the dead Content Creator JavaScript (~485 lines) that referenced UI elements not present in the free plugin.
  • Removed the artificial 5-post bulk-update cap. Bulk refresh now runs whatever count you select; a confirmation prompt warns about API usage when 10+ posts are selected.
  • Comprehensive output-escaping pass: all admin output now uses esc_html(), esc_attr(), esc_url(), wp_kses_post(), or intval() as appropriate. Removed blanket phpcs:disable WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput.OutputNotEscaped suppression comments.
  • Added cleanup of legacy options on uninstall.

2.3.36

  • Fixed output escaping in welcome notice (WP.org Plugin Check compliance)

2.3.35

  • Removed setup wizard — replaced with a simple one-line admin notice on first activation
  • Removed all license/trialware references for WP.org compliance
  • Fixed escaping in metabox and admin UI

2.3.34

  • WordPress.org free version — unlimited refreshes, no license required
  • Removed article creator (available in Pro at contentrefreshai.com)
  • Removed auto-scheduler (available in Pro)
  • Fixed all escaping issues flagged by Plugin Check
  • Removed Freemius SDK dependency
  • Refactored goto statements, error_log calls, and slow DB queries
